sentences.text: "I can't lift baby Shanu," says Abbu. "You are too small."
"You can't walk to school alone," says Ammi. "You are too small."
"You can't sleep in the baby's cot," says Dadu. "You are too big."
"You can't carry the baby to the park," says Dadi. "You are too big."
Shanu is puzzled. Too big! Too small!
How can she be too big and too small all at once?
"You are just the right size to be our little girl," says Dadi with a warm hug.
"Ammachi, could we make coconut barfi today?" asks Sooraj.
"Only if you help me pick the coconuts," says Ammachi.
Ammachi ties a pulley around the tree trunk.
She steps into the loop and uses her seat to climb up smoothly.
"Ready, Sooraj? Catch the ripe ones!" she calls out.
Thud! A big brown coconut falls right into the soft grass.
Back in the kitchen, Ammachi attaches an old bicycle crank to the coconut scraper.
She pedals happily, and sweet white flakes fly into the wooden bowl.
Soon, the aroma of sweet coconut barfi fills the entire house.

title: The Girl Who Could Not Stop Laughing

sentences.text: Tsering was a cheerful young girl who lived in a quiet mountain village in Ladakh.
One sunny morning, she heard a funny noise coming from the yak shed.
When she peeked inside, a little goat was wearing a woolly hat, chewing on a dandelion.
Tsering burst into giggles, and soon she could not stop laughing at all.
At school, her teacher tried to maintain silence during the history lesson.
But every time Tsering remembered the goat in the woolly hat, she let out another loud chuckle.
The giggles were contagious, spreading from one desk to another across the classroom.
By lunchtime, even the stern village elder had a wide grin on his weathered face.
Tsering realized that while silence has its place, laughter is the true sunshine of the valley.
High above the sun-drenched plains of central India, a solitary wanderer gazed yearningly towards the distant snow-capped Himalayas.
Exiled far from his beloved companion, he yearned to send her word of his unwavering devotion.
As the monsoon approached, a majestic storm cloud gathered above the jagged mountain ridge, heavy with rain and promise.
"Noble messenger of the skies," the wanderer whispered, "carry my thoughts across rivers, emerald valleys, and ancient temples."
The dark cloud rumbled in gentle acknowledgment, casting cool shadows over the parched landscape below.
Journeying northward on the winds of destiny, it promised to bridge the silent distance between two separated hearts.
